chunks: And ‘Āṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله sent ‘Alī عليه السلام to Yemen, and when he returned, he said to him: “Tell me of the most astonishing matter that came before you.”

He said: “O Messenger of Allah, some people came to me who had jointly bought a slave-girl, then they all had intercourse with her in one period of purity, and she gave birth to a boy. They disputed regarding him, each of them claiming him. So I cast lots among them, three times, and assigned him to the one whose lot came out, and I made him liable for their shares.”
Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: “There is no people who draw lots and entrust their affair to Allah except that the lot of the one who is in the right comes forth.”

key_terms.الْمُحِقِّ: the one who is rightfully correct
key_terms.تَبَايَعُوا: entered into a mutual purchase or shared transaction
key_terms.سَهْمُهُ: his lot or allotted share in the draw
key_terms.ضَمَّنْتُهُ: I made him liable or responsible

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about drawing lots in disputed legal cases?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a judicial case judged by Imam ‘Alī عليه السلام concerning disputed paternity after shared ownership of a slave-girl. It affirms the legitimacy of drawing lots in difficult contested matters when the affair is entrusted to Allah, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله approved this judgment.
